item.title: 8 Iconic Video Game Villains Who Were Actually Right the Whole Time
item.description: Grab your gavel: Court is in session for eight of gaming’s most misunderstood villains. Their charges? One occupied planet, one erased painting, one underwater utopia gone to rot, and a truly staggering body count. But, all that aside, what if these bad guys were actually making a somewhat decent point? Read between the lines of their melodramatic monologues, and perhaps you’ll realize that, say, a centuries-long guilt trip over one catastrophic mistake was in fact understandable rationale for wanting to tear the world down and start over. Or not: You get to decide. Just read each villain’s case file below before reaching a verdict — you might not love where the evidence actually points.

item.title: GTA 6 Players Report Issues with Physical Version Pre-Order Codes
item.description: With its launch less than a week away, players all over the world have started preloading Grand Theft Auto 6 to ensure they're able to play as soon as it drops. Reports from several fans indicate that some code-in-box copies of GTA 6 include a faulty redemption leaflet, preventing buyers from claiming the game.

item.title: 10 Near-Perfect Nintendo Switch Games Nobody Played
item.description: When a system has a library as diverse as the Nintendo Switch, some great games are bound to go unrecognized. There are thousands of physical titles available, and thousands more that never got more than a simple digital release. Not every game is for everyone, though. Many players choose to ignore the digital marketplace altogether because it has become so cluttered. We sometimes overlook even physical releases, now that there are so many of them. That means there are plenty of hidden gems to discover, especially when it comes to the stuff you won’t find on any other console. With that in mind, here are 10 near-perfect Switch games nobody played.

item.title: James Gunn Responds To Scathing Man of Tomorrow Rumors Following DC Studios Exit
item.description: Skydance's decision to replace DC Studios heads James Gunn and Peter Safran with Jeremy Latcham earlier this week has spawned all sorts of rumors and reports. For the first time since the news broke last Monday, James Gunn spoke out on social media to deny certain rumors, specifically those surrounding next year's Superman sequel, Man of Tomorrow .

item.title: Netflix’s New KPop Demon Hunters Replacement Is an Instant Fantasy Classic
item.description: A quarter-century after Shrek first married the princess and turned the entire genre on its head, these subverted fairytales have become about as commonplace as the original stories that inspired them. So when Netflix announced a new animated movie told from the perspectives of Cinderella's Ugly Stepsisters, it wasn't exactly an inspired choice. Disney already did that two decades ago with Cinderella II: Dreams Come True (2002) and Cinderella III: A Twist in Time (2007), with a live-action film following the unlikable duo set for release in the future.

item.title: Pokémon Go 'Streets to Skies' choose a path — steel or dragon?
item.description: As part of the ticketed bonus to Pokémon Go 's 2026 Wild Area event , players can start a set of Special Research Tasks called "Streets to Skies." During this research, you'll need to pick between steel- or dragon-type Pokémon , with your pick having a slight impact on your rewards.

item.title: Ubisoft Is Reportedly Bringing A Beloved Series Back After Nearly Two Decades
item.description: Before Rainbow Six Siege , Ubisoft published two Rainbow Six: Vegas games for PS3 and Xbox 360. Now, a new report suggests that a third Rainbow Six: Vegas game is in the works, moving the franchise beyond Siege .

item.title: Magic: The Gathering’s 5 Best and Weirdest Star Trek References
item.description: Magic: The Gathering ’s Star Trek is a love letter to the franchise. The set uses sagas to pay tribute to standout episodes like “ The Inner Light ” and “In the Pale Moonlight,” and it’s stuffed with cards representing legendary characters and spacecraft along with famous quotes like “Live long and prosper.” But the set also features plenty of deeper cuts, embracing the times that Star Trek was silly, controversial, and downright terrible. These are the five best references to the franchise’s worst and weirdest moments.

item.title: Big Walk's AI Controversy Overshadows a Remarkable Creative Achievement
item.description: And then we took Kalonica [Quigley] in, who's now the fifth member of House House, and gave her a tour of this island. It was much smaller than the final thing, but it was really just an island with a bunch of trees and a few rocks, and maybe the red lookout tower was there, or an earlier version of it. There was a giant floating sphere and maybe just some really primitive shapes. But we took her around and had this really amazing experience just exploring together. It felt social and fun, like hanging out with your friends.

item.title: Pluribus Season 2 Makes One Of Its Best Characters A Series Regular
item.description: As the second season of Apple TV's Pluribus enters production, more details are emerging. On Nov. 13, we learned that a standout cast member from the show's first season will be promoted to a series regular.
